---
title: "Difference-in-Differences: Staggered Adoption and TWFE Bias"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

## Motivation

Many empirical settings feature staggered adoption, where different units receive treatment at different points in time.
The standard two-way fixed effects (TWFE) DiD estimator is commonly applied in such settings.

However, recent research shows that TWFE may produce biased and misleading estimates under staggered treatment timing.

## Simulated Panel with Staggered Treatment

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

n_units <- 90
time_periods <- 1:12

panel <- expand.grid(
  id = 1:n_units,
  time = time_periods
) %>%
  mutate(
    treat_time = case_when(
      id <= 30 ~ 5,
      id <= 60 ~ 8,
      TRUE ~ Inf
    ),
    treated = ifelse(time >= treat_time, 1, 0),
    outcome = 2 + 0.3 * time +
      2 * treated +
      rnorm(n(), sd = 0.7)
  )
```

## Two-Way Fixed Effects DiD

We estimate the standard TWFE DiD regression using unit and time fixed effects.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(fixest)

twfe <- feols(
  outcome ~ treated | id + time,
  data = panel
)

twfe
```

## Why TWFE Can Be Misleading

With staggered adoption, treated units serve as controls for later-treated units.
As a result, the TWFE estimator implicitly compares already-treated units to newly treated units.

This can induce negative or inappropriate weights, even when treatment effects are homogeneous.

## Intuition: Forbidden Comparisons

Comparisons between treated and not-yet-treated units are valid.
Comparisons where treated units act as controls for other treated units are not.

TWFE does not distinguish between these comparisons.

## Implications

Event-study plots based on TWFE may also be misleading in staggered settings.

This motivates the use of modern DiD estimators designed for staggered adoption.


## Looking Ahead

The limitations of the two-way fixed effects estimator in staggered adoption settings raise an important question:
how should difference-in-differences be implemented when treatment timing varies across units?

Recent methodological advances propose alternative estimators that explicitly account for treatment timing
and avoid the forbidden comparisons implicit in TWFE.

The next chapter introduces these modern difference-in-differences estimators and shows how they resolve
the problems highlighted here.
